rawFindings.title: Falsy subpath values prevent array atomics from being converted to $set
rawFindings.explanation: This new guard returns when the later dirty subpath's current value is falsy. For document arrays, a modified subdocument path can become `undefined` after an element is pulled, but the parent array still has atomics and must be converted to a full `$set` to preserve both the pull and the subdocument edit. Skipping that conversion leaves only the array pull atomic, so the subdocument field change is not persisted.
rawFindings.suggestion: Do not require `item.value` to be truthy. For example, change this guard to `if (!top.value) return;` or restore the `top.value && top.value._atomics` check before accessing atomics.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Given a document with `comments: [{body:'a'}, {body:'b'}, {body:'c'}]`, load it, set `comments[2].body = 'changed'`, then call `comments.pull(comments[1])` and save. The saved document ends up with `[{body:'a'}, {body:'c'}]` instead of preserving `[{body:'a'}, {body:'changed'}]`.
